reason: Both conversations correctly deliver the critical safety stop (unplug, don't use, engineer to inspect) and neither asks the sensible follow-up questions about smoke, lint filter or vent hose. Conversation 2 edges ahead by explicitly forbidding a test run ('not even as a test'), telling the owner to let it cool, and giving an honest, hedged picture of likely causes (lint on the heater element vs an electrical fault) without claiming it is 'just fluff' or naming a failed part. Its repetition is a minor stylistic weakness, but the extra safety-relevant specificity serves the homeowner slightly better than Conversation 1's bare warning.
